WorkDetail: Work previously approved under #392820. Mixed-use first floor retail and residential above with 82 residential units and one level of subgrade parking. Please note that sheet C-102 shows that an existing street closure was processed for Burnham Place between Parkside Place and Kenilworth Terrace NE in 2009 and is currently private property. The existing curb cut alignments in public space are being modified to decrease in width. Burnham Place will be one-way circulation from south to north. Private Burnham Place will also hold loading activities as well as garage entry. This project proposes all DDOT standard streetscape elements. No non-standard elements are proposed in public space. As discussed in the PDRM held on 3/8/2022, public space along Parkside Place NE is not wide enough to accommodate both the minimum tree box width of 4 ft and the minimum ADA width of 6 ft. The project proposes the minimum street tree box width of 4 ft and the remaining width to building face (including less than 1 ft into private property) will maintain clear sidewalk width for pedestrians. Parkside Place curb cut proposes a replacement of the existing eastern ADA ramp and a proposed receiving ADA ramp and crosswalk for pedestrians given surrounding intersection and as-built conditions. Kenilworth Terrace proposes a receiving ADA ramp for approved and issued permit #358092.

WorkDetail: The existing curb cut/driveway on 3rd St NE shall be removed/closed with new DDOT curb and gutter.  The existing concrete apron shall be converted into DDOT scored sidewalk.  In addition, a 42" chain link fence shall be installed on private property within the 15' Building Restriction Line for security for the proposed school.  Bike racks shall also be installed within the building restriction line.  A lead walk on the Kennedy St NE side shall also be installed for ADA access.  There will be the removal of a 14" American Sycamore (Platanus Occidentalis) on the Kennedy St NE side and the planting of a replacement American Sycamore nearby, which is included in this application.  The site has a previously approved Special Tree Removal permit #TA90669 for the special site trees to be removed, which has been extended.  There is also an offsite hazardous special tree at 300 Hamilton St NE that will be impacted by the development and special tree removal permit  #TA95939 was also obtained. A Tree Preservation Plan was also submitted to TOPs under tracking #96604 due to the impact of the proposed leadwalk and sidewalk extension on the existing special trees.

WorkDetail:
POLE RESTORATION: Trinidad Avenue NE and Public Alley
•	We will excavate a hole as wide as diameter of the pole and about 8 inches away from the pole.
•	We then hand dig down to a depth of 36 – 60 inches.
•	Using Non-Conductive soil probes, probing in areas where soil cannot be unearthed.
•	A steel truss is then placed in the hole, against the pole.
•	Using a fiberglass support pole, a pneumatic jack hammer is raised to a height of about 8 Ft.
•	Using the jack hammer, the truss is driven into the ground at total depth of 5 to 5.5 feet deep depending on pole size.
•	The truss is then banded to the pole in two locations. The first location 15 to 26 inches above groundline and at 50-55 inches above groundline at the top of the truss.
•	The removed dirt will be replaced. The surrounding work area will be cleaned of other debris and unused installation material
•	A cap will then be placed over the top of the truss.
•	The truss is then painted with a cold galvanizing compound paint to prevent corrosion.

WorkDetail:
The following is a list of stormwater reduction practices or technologies that are permitted to be installed on public space as part of the 
Program: A. Rain Barrels as defined as a large container, generally five feet (5’) in height, used to capture and store the rainwater running 
through a downspout from the roof. Rain Barrel installations taller than seven feet (7’) shall not be installed on public space. The overflow 
from rain barrels installed on public space and authorized by this MOU should lead to the same collection point as did the original 
downspout. Rain Barrels shall not be installed on public space at the front of properties in historic districts unless there is sufficient space for 
screening and/or to be contained within the landscape. B. Rain Gardens as defined as a small garden landscaped to collect, store and 
infiltrate stormwater runoff in its loose amended soil and strategically placed to intercept stormwater runoff until it can be fully absorbed 
into the ground. Rain gardens authorized by this MOU shall not contain underdrains that connect to sewer lines in public space. C. Pervious 
pavement as defined as any paved surface that permits water to soak naturally into the ground to replace existing impervious surfaces. At 
properties where no public sidewalks exist, existing lead walks and driveways may be replaced with pervious pavement between the 
property line and the curb line of the roadway subject to the terms of the RiverSmart Homes Maintenance Agreement (“Maintenance 
Agreement”) as provided below. D. Shade Trees as defined as a large tree with a widespread, dense canopy. A selection of shade trees native 
to the Chesapeake Bay region has been chosen by DDOE that will benefit homeowners as well as the local watersheds. E. Bayscaping as 
defined by vegetation that is native to the Chesapeake Bay region to replace existing lawn area. Template Bayscaping gardens have been 
developed by DDOE that will benefit homeowners and reduce pollution to local watersheds.
